newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels accuse army of shooting civilians.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels accuse army of shooting civilians.

text.p: Separatist Tamil Tiger rebels on Monday accused the Sri Lankan army of shooting minority Tamil civilians in retaliation for the killing of a policeman by rebels.

Three civilians were killed and seven wounded when soldiers opened fire at people decorating the town of Valachchenai, 240 km (150 miles) east of Colombo, to honour a dead rebel sympathiser, the rebels' official Voice of Tigers radio said.
The radio said the soldiers opened fire after the rebels shot and killed a policeman who tried to stop people putting up the decorations.
A military spokesman in Colombo told Reuters he was unaware of the reported shooting.
The decorations were planned to honour Annai Poopathy, a Tamil woman who died nine years ago after fasting in protest against India's involvement in Sri Lanka's ethnic war.

"It was a retaliatory attack by soldiers. They opened fire indiscriminately at civilians. Those injured lay without assistance for half an hour while heavily armed soldiers and police roamed the area," the rebel radio said.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), who are fighting for an independent homeland for Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, regard Annai Poopathy as a martyr.
She died protesting against Indian armed forces who were sent by New Delhi in 1987 to disarm the LTTE under a controversial pact signed between the two governments.
Indian troops were withdrawn in mid-1990 after suffering heavy casualties and failing to defeat the Tigers.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the number is higher.
